title: Vitest Examples
description: Small Vitest examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Your first Vitest check
examples.description: Vitest runs named tests and reports mismatched expectations. It works with JavaScript and TypeScript projects.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("counts apples", () => { expect(3 + 2).toBe(5); });

examples.title: Object equality
examples.description: toEqual compares the values inside an object. It is useful when a function returns a new object.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("returns a point", () => { const point = { x: 2, y: 4 }; expect(point).toEqual({ x: 2, y: 4 }); });

examples.title: Partial object checks
examples.description: objectContaining checks selected fields when other fields are not part of the current test.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("has a title", () => { expect({ title: "Moon", pages: 24 }).toEqual(expect.objectContaining({ title: "Moon" })); });

examples.title: Parameterized tests
examples.description: test.each repeats one rule for a table of examples. This reduces repeated test code while keeping cases visible.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test.each([[1, 1], [2, 4], [3, 9]])("square %i", (input, expected) => { expect(input * input).toBe(expected); });

examples.title: Fresh fixtures
examples.description: A fixture is prepared data used by a test. beforeEach can give each test a new fixture.

examples.title: Function spies
examples.description: vi.fn creates a spy that records its calls. You can check the arguments as well as the count.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("notifies with score", () => { const notify = vi.fn(); notify(7); expect(notify).toHaveBeenCalledWith(7); });

examples.title: Restore a spied method
examples.description: vi.spyOn watches an existing method. Restore it after the test so later code sees the normal method again.

examples.title: Async assertions
examples.description: Use await when checking a promise. The test must stay active until the check is finished.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("reads a label", async () => { const load = async () => "ready"; await expect(load()).resolves.toBe("ready"); });

examples.title: Expected rejected work
examples.description: A failing promise can be the correct result for invalid input. rejects tests that case explicitly.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("missing book", async () => { await expect(Promise.reject(new Error("No book"))).rejects.toThrow("No book"); });

examples.title: Fake time
examples.description: Vitest can replace timers with a controlled clock. This makes a timer test quick and repeatable.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("waits for reminder", () => { vi.useFakeTimers(); try { const remind = vi.fn(); setTimeout(remind, 500); vi.advanceTimersByTime(500); expect(remind).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1); } finally { vi.useRealTimers(); } });

examples.title: DOM tests need an environment
examples.description: A Node test has no real browser page. Choose a DOM test environment or browser mode when the behaviour needs page elements.

examples.title: Use coverage as a clue
examples.description: Coverage reports which code was reached by tests. Reaching a line does not prove its result was checked well.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("both signs", () => { const positive = n => n > 0; expect(positive(2)).toBe(true); expect(positive(-1)).toBe(false); });
